claim: In Gravesend, by ablation before a blind reviewer, what made a shopfront say what it is: the lettered name was decisive (it turned a 'dress shop' into a pawnbroker and a 'storeroom' into a grocer); a surround (reveal, fascia over the window head, pilasters between sashes) helped because the sign needs something to sit on; taking the light out of the display hurt mildly, because it hid the goods; and goods that do not fit the trade contradicted the sign.
evidence: projects/blood-city/experiments/shop-surrounds/README.md and critic.md (2026-11-18): what-if.png and before-after.png, five unlabelled sets; projects/blood-city/tests/test_whatif.py ShopSurroundTests
letter sprites (tiles 3808-3833) under a parallax sky: E1M4 33, E3M1 0 (recounted 2026-11-26); DukCity 38 to 73 counted 2026-11-17, not recounted
use: Name first (glass.write_names on a fascia), then the surround (glass.surround, stand pilasters after the lintel pass or one pilaster repaints the jambs), then goods of the trade. Fascia lettering is not legible from across a street; cut a chain lamp to a low display.

checked.how: Read projects/blood-city/experiments/shop-surrounds/README.md and critic.md: sign 'decisive ... turns the pawn from a dress shop into a pawnbroker and the super from a storeroom into a grocer'; surround helps ('the sign has nothing to sit on'); unlit 'hurts, mildly ... hides the goods' - not 'barely matters'; unlit removed 10 lit sectors and 6 lamps, not a lamp alone. ShopSurroundTests is in projects/blood-city/tests/test_whatif.py:157, not tests/. Recounted letter sprites 3808-3833 under a parallax sky (work script): E1M4 33, E3M1 0; DukCity not recounted.
